measurement_notes: Fractions of the full 2688x1520 frame. screen_corners: as seen, top = the far long edge, so top_left is the far-left corner (the phone's top end, away from the port) and bottom_right is the near-right corner. They are the intersections of straight lines fitted to the four edges of the black glass inside the red lip (residual under 3 px), i.e. the sharp-corner quad for a matrix3d map. The visible rounded corners sit just inside them: apexes about (0.532, 0.655), (0.729, 0.747), (0.659, 0.805), (0.459, 0.701). window_glass_polygon: order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. The left inner edge is at x 1652 px, the right at 2637 px, and the bottom at y 851 px on the left and 861 px on the right. The table far edge is at y 0.600; the phone case bbox is x 0.4505-0.7381, y 0.6507-0.8447.
notes: Zero defects at any severity. Deviations from the spec boxes were measured and judged harmless for the web build. The phone is about 29% wide, not 22%, and starts at x 0.45, but it stays out of the headline zone and keeps every margin. The window opening runs off the top edge and the table edge sits at 0.600, not 0.63. Note for the build: the plate's aspect is 1.768, the generator's 2k 16:9 size, not exactly 1.778, which is irrelevant under object-fit cover. The far layer behind the keyed window must extend above the frame's top edge by the parallax travel, because the opening has no top rail to hide it.
